title: Lenny Rachitsky: the race car growth framework (engines, boosts, lubricants, fuel) and early users
summary: Lenny lays out his race car framework for long-term growth: pick one of four self-sustaining engines (performance marketing, virality, content, sales), then layer turbo boosts and lubricants. He also covers getting the first users, retention benchmarks, and how he built his newsletter to 55k free and 5k paid subscribers.

principles.text: Only four engines drive long-term growth: performance marketing, virality, content, sales. Become best in the world at one.
principles.quote: it turns out there's essentially four engines you can choose from as a company and uh and these engines are self-sustaining loops that keep your business growing

principles.text: Spreading effort across many channels rarely works. Concentrate on one engine, add a second only when the first plateaus.
principles.quote: you have to become really really good at one to any chance and often people kind of spread their resources too thin

principles.text: Anticipate the S-curve plateau and plant the next engine early, building a layer cake of growth.
principles.quote: you want to anticipate this plateau approaching at some near future and start to plant seeds for another engine

principles.text: Performance marketing fits only if users pay you immediately and nobody is searching for your product. Otherwise avoid building on it.
principles.quote: you need to be generating revenue from your users immediately so that you can feed that right back into the ads and then two is your product is not something people are naturally looking for

principles.text: Measure virality by the share of new users arriving via friends or referral; well over half signals a real viral engine.
principles.quote: look at the percentage of your new users who came in through a referral or a word of mouth

principles.text: Early on, do non-scalable turbo boosts to ignite the engine: reach out to your 'customers who care' and find them directly.
principles.quote: early on most of your work is should be these boosts which kind of ignite the engine a little bit like reaching out to strangers to get them to try your thing
